title: Unauthenticated loopback agent channel: any local process can inject fabricated SQL events, seize capture control, suppress attach, and eavesdrop on the agent's SQL frames
description: The IDE-agent IPC channel has no peer authentication in either direction. The IDE's loopback ServerSockets (attach chain AgentManager.kt:799, premain channels :899, re-bind :1577-1581) accept any local connection and turn it into a full AgentSession whose frames are treated as agent-authoritative; session identity is a self-reported HELLO pid. Consequences for a malicious local process: (1) inject fabricated SQL events that flow into the same sinks as console lines (panel, autosave files with attacker-chosen provenance headers, jump-to-source navigation, history and dialect inference); (2) spoof CMD_CONFIG_ACK to control SqlCaptureGate.paused (suppress the console bridge or fake 'agent confirmed active'), and poison attachedPids with a chosen pid to suppress attach of real targets; (3) receive the agent's EVENT frames (SQL text and literal parameter values) by winning the port race, sustaining the stream past the 15s watchdog with a forged CONFIG. Verified as strongest source-visible controls on this path: loopback-only bind, 1MB frame caps (AgentProtocol.kt:41, SenderLoop.java:53), capture-state/user-pause gates (AgentSessionSupport.kt:513,538), per-pid HELLO dedup (AgentManager.kt:1156-1160), and SenderLoop MAX_FAST_DROPS (SenderLoop.java:112) — all are capture-state, rate, or per-pid mechanisms, none is a peer-identity check; no token, shared secret, HMAC, OS peer credential, or remote-address check exists in either the IDE-side (src/main/kotlin/.../log/agent/) or agent-side (sub-projects/sql-visualizer-agent) code, and the negotiated port is passed to the target JVM with no capability secret (AgentProtocol.kt:67-68). The decisive OS-level facts (which local adversary model applies, loopback reachability across users, port discovery) were not locally observable in this source-only run.
claimed_root_cause: AgentManager binds loopback ServerSockets (AgentManager.kt:799 attach, :899 premain, :1577-1581 re-bind) and grants every accepted connection full session authority with no OS peer credential, shared secret, or channel-ownership check; HELLO pid (AgentManager.kt:157, :1196-1210) is self-reported and trusted for attachedPids registration (AgentManager.kt:1162) and premain channel pid; AgentSession.handleFrame (AgentSessionSupport.kt:486-588) applies EVENT/HEARTBEAT/CONFIG_ACK frames from any connected socket to the panel/autosave/navigation sinks and the SqlCaptureGate bridge gate; agent-side SenderLoop (SenderLoop.java:225) unconditionally writes HELLO/HEARTBEAT/EVENT frames (SQL + literal parameter values) to whatever answers the negotiated port and applies inbound CONFIG from that peer (SenderLoop.java:429-471).

trace.description: Loopback accept loop accepts any local TCP connection to the premain/attach port; no peer credential, token, or origin check exists between accept() and session creation (verified: no getRemoteSocketAddress/peer-credential/remote-address check anywhere in log/agent/).

Session identity is established from the self-reported HELLO body; the digits-only regex accepts any attacker-chosen non-negative pid, and a missing/malformed HELLO yields pid=0 which is still tolerated (session committed at :1161, only the attachedPids registration at :1162 is skipped); the session is committed under sessionCommitLock with attachedPids[pid] registered (:1150-1163) regardless of who the peer actually is; the per-pid dedup at :1156-1160 only drops a duplicate of an already-healthy same-pid session, so any other chosen pid is accepted.

EVENT/HEARTBEAT/CONFIG_ACK frames from the unauthenticated socket are honored; the only pre-sink gates are capture-state (listenActiveProvider :513) and user pause (:538), not peer identity; spoofed EVENT is adapted by AgentEventAdapter.toEntry (:523) with fully attacker-chosen sql/params/sourceFile/sourceCandidates/url (AgentEvent.kt:11,21,25,35,39).

Fabricated SQL entry enters the panel/autosave/jump-to-source chain identically to console-captured lines; spoofed sourceFile is written verbatim into the autosave header (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:488-490) and spoofed sourceCandidates drive editor navigation (EntryJumpResolver.kt:33-53).

title: Imported dynamic-table-name regex rules are compiled and executed with no complexity or timeout bound on the preview render path
description: DynamicTableNameProcessor compiles each rule pattern with Regex(pattern) and runs regex.find(tableName) (DynamicTableNameProcessor.kt:39) on every wrapper preview render, with no timeout, input-length bound, or complexity screen. dynamicTableNameRules is one of the fields an imported settings file can set, so a shared file can install a catastrophic-backtracking pattern (nested quantifiers over alternation) that hangs the preview render when the operator previews any statement whose table name triggers the pathological path — an availability effect reaching beyond the file author. The regex result cache is also an unsynchronized mutableMapOf (line 26) that can be read during render and cleared by PluginCacheManager.clearAll (PluginCacheManager.kt:33) from another thread.
claimed_root_cause: User/importer-supplied regex from settings is executed on the render path without a ReDoS bound (no timeout, no pattern screening, no input cap) and the compile cache is unsynchronized.

title: Dependency resolution prefers the Aliyun mirror over Maven Central with no dependency verification, so substituted mirror bytes flow into the shipped plugin unchallenged
description: settings.gradle.kts declares https://maven.aliyun.com/repository/public (line 50) before mavenCentral (line 52) in dependencyResolutionManagement, and Gradle resolves each module from the first repository that contains it. There is no gradle/verification-metadata.xml (verified: gradle/ contains only libs.versions.toml, plugin-change-notes.html and wrapper/), so no artifact checksum is enforced anywhere in the build. CI hardening steps (five occurrences in build-plugin.yml) strip only proxy properties and rewrite the Gradle wrapper URL, leaving the dependency mirror active. The sole runtime dependency, com.github.jsqlparser:jsqlparser:5.3, is therefore resolved through this priority chain and its bytes are packed into build/distributions/*.zip, uploaded as the plugin artifact and published to GitHub Releases and the Gitee beta self-update channel (update/update.json downloadUrl). Whoever can influence what the mirror serves for these coordinates (mirror operator compromise, mirror-to-Central drift) reaches executed plugin code without any integrity check noticing.
claimed_root_cause: Repository resolution order grants a third-party mirror priority over the canonical Maven Central while the build defines no dependency verification (checksums/signatures), so the intended control (Central as trusted root) is bypassed by configuration rather than compromised.

title: Gradle wrapper distribution is fetched from the Tencent mirror with no distributionSha256Sum, so local builds (including the Gitee beta release build) run an unverified toolchain

title: ExecutionTimeParser trailing-ms regex backtracks quadratically over whitespace runs on unbounded console lines
description: finishEntries runs ExecutionTimeParser.parse on the full, untruncated console line of every entry-producing line (both the normal processConsoleLine exit at SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:1170 and the sniffed-unseal exit at :1114). TRAILING_MS_REGEX = [\]\s]\s*(\d+)\s*ms\s*$ (MULTILINE, ExecutionTimeParser.kt:36) begins with a character class that matches every space, so on a whitespace-heavy line the engine retries at every whitespace index and greedily consumes then backtracks through the entire remaining whitespace run: O(run length^2) per whitespace run, i.e. quadratic in line length. A single ~500KB padded line (e.g. '==> Parameters: 1(Long)' followed by hundreds of KB of spaces) from a hosted process costs a superlinear number of engine steps per line on the parse thread.
claimed_root_cause: A hot-path duration regex whose leading token is an unanchored whitespace-matching character class is applied to full unbounded console lines; unlike the parsers' maxParseLength-bound SQL bodies, the line passed to ExecutionTimeParser.parse is never truncated.

title: Token-less log lines share one fallback parser bucket, restoring cross-thread Preparing/Parameters mispairing that reaches SQL execution
description: Thread bucketing - the fix for concurrent parameter mispairing - fails open when threadTokenOf cannot extract a token: such lines route to a single shared fallback bucket with single-slot pendingSql/pendingParams state (LogThreadRouter.kt:45,117). Two threads logging bare '==> Preparing:'/'==> Parameters:' lines (no log-framework level keyword, typical of stdout MyBatis logging) interleave in that one bucket. Source reconstruction of the deterministic interleaving A-Preparing(a), B-Preparing(b), A-Parameters(1), B-Parameters(9): B's Preparing closes A's statement parameterless (branch-1 closePending), A's Parameters then pairs with B's pendingSql producing an entry 'b restored with A's values' (branch 4 at MyBatisLogParser.kt:138 + closePending:194 + positional restorer.restore), and B's Parameters is dropped (paramWithoutContext). The console-capture variant surfaces this mispaired restoredSql in SqlLogPanel and in export (SqlLogPanelActions.kt:108 is the export row build); the execution boundary is LogToSqlPanel, which feeds pasted log text through the same MyBatisLogParser/LogThreadRouter fail-open path (LogToSqlPanel.kt:490-491) and sends the converted statements to SqlExecutor.execute (LogToSqlPanel.kt:302/323 -> executeSql:340 -> SqlExecutor.execute:359), i.e. SQL executes with parameter values from a different statement (DML confirm and dialect gate remain, but the user cannot detect the mispairing from the confirmed SQL text).

title: MyBatis/Hibernate parser thread buckets are never evicted while pending, accumulating unbounded retained SQL per console
description: LogThreadRouter caps buckets at 64 (DEFAULT_MAX_BUCKETS) but evictIdle removes only isIdle buckets. A MyBatisLogParser bucket that received a Preparing:/bare-SQL line without a closing Parameters line holds pendingSql (up to maxParseLength=20000 chars, plus the untruncated pendingLogLine raw line) or prefixMatched/paramPrefixMatched wait state and is therefore never idle (isIdle at MyBatisLogParser.kt:65 requires pendingSql == null && !prefixMatched && !paramPrefixMatched). HibernateLogParser.feedIdle equivalently sets collecting=true. Unlike JdbcTemplate and ShardingSphere parsers, MyBatisLogParser and HibernateLogParser have no flushSettled: source-wide grep confirmed flushSettled/settledBuckets is invoked only for jdbcParser and shardingParser (SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:1165-1166 in the per-line path and :453/:467 in the EDT-periodic flushSettledEntries), and the capture path never calls ctx.myBatisParser.closePending()/ctx.hibernateParser.closePending() (closePending() callers are only LogToSqlPanel and SqlVisualizerRenderLogsTool, each on its own parser instances). So each unique thread token that printed one unclosed statement retains its SQL text for the life of the console: sustained log volume with varying thread names grows retained memory linearly with total printed SQL volume while the IDE console cycle buffer discards the same text.

title: MCP read-only execution guard is client-side only: SELECT-invoked server-side side effects execute with full datasource privileges while sqlv_explain advertises readOnlyHint=TRUE
description: sqlv_explain tells the MCP agent the tool is strictly read-only (@McpToolHints readOnlyHint=TRUE at SqlVisualizerExplainTool.kt:30 and description 'Strictly read-only ... rejections are fail-closed' at lines 26-27). The actual control is McpSelectGuard.checkSingleSelect — a client-side statement-shape and keyword filter that by design admits any single plain SELECT — followed by McpDbExecutor connecting to the project datasource with its stored credentials and executing the statement without any database-layer read-only enforcement (repo-wide grep of src/main finds no connection.setReadOnly, no SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, and no session read-only init). A statement that passes the guard as a plain SELECT can still cause server-side writes and state changes through SELECT-invoked functions and stored routines (user-defined functions performing DML; engine builtins such as MySQL load_file(), PostgreSQL pg_read_file/pg_ls_dir/lo_import/dblink/pg_sleep), and through planner-time function evaluation, all with the datasource account's full privileges. The guard's own deny-list (McpSelectGuard.kt:37-45, verified FORBIDDEN_WORDS) covers statement verbs, not function bodies, and no downstream layer narrows the account's authority.
claimed_root_cause: McpSelectGuard enforces read-only as a purely client-side syntactic property (single plain SELECT), and McpDbExecutor.executeQuery never places the connection or session in a read-only mode (no setReadOnly, no read-only transaction start), so the guarantee communicated to the agent (readOnlyHint TRUE) exceeds what any layer in this repository enforces; the effective authority is the datasource account's full privilege set.

description: The custom OGNL evaluator used for <if test>, <bind value>, ${} and foreach collection expressions degrades all parse failures to ParseResult.Err and all evaluation-time failures to EvalResult.Err — but only OgnlParseException is caught in parseUncached (Ognl.kt:133-137) and evaluate(text) calls parse() outside the Throwable-guarded AST evaluator (Ognl.kt:153-157; the KDoc at :152 scopes its degradation promise to evaluation time 求值期, while parse() itself presents ParseResult.Err as its only caller-facing failure mode and every helper built on parse assumes it does not throw). title: Lower-trust strings interpolated unescaped into HTML-enabled Swing labels and tooltips in rollback dialog, preview meta line, and error tooltip
description: The plugin renders lower-trust text (SQL fragments restored from console capture, mapper XML statement identifiers, DB-server error text) through Swing HTML labels. title: Update zip guard bounds sizes and counts but delegates entry-name sanitization (zip-slip, Windows reserved names) entirely to unverified platform extractors
description: UpdateZipGuard.check, the plugin-side control at the archive/install boundary, validates only entry counts and declared/actual sizes; it never inspects entry.name. Actual extraction is performed by platform code: StartupActionScriptManager.UnzipCommand on the restart-script path and the unpack inside PluginInstaller.installAndLoadDynamicPlugin on the dynamic path. Neither extractor's canonicalization behavior (rejection of ../ and nested .., absolute or drive-qualified targets, NTFS colon/alternate-data-stream names, reserved device names such as CON/NUL, trailing dots/spaces on Windows, duplicate entry names) is visible in this repository, and no repo test exercises extraction of a traversal-named or Windows-hostile entry name. If either platform extractor writes entries by raw name, a channel-controlled update zip writes files outside the plugins root or into hostile file names on the developer's machine at install time (restart-script path executes at next IDE startup with no re-validation).
claimed_root_cause: The component that guarantees archive bounds (UpdateZipGuard) does not validate the property the consumer relies on (safe entry paths); the extraction components that would enforce it are platform code whose guarantee is assumed, not verified, and the restart-script path re-executes the persisted zip at next startup without re-running any guard.

title: Update artifact plugin-id gate uses a regex that XML comments can desync from the platform descriptor parser
description: DynamicInstallSupport.validateArtifact is the sole control binding a downloaded update zip to this plugin's identity before installation. It extracts <id> with the regex <id>(.*?)</id> (DOT_MATCHES_ALL) over the raw plugin.xml text, which matches tag content inside XML comments, whereas the platform descriptor loader used for the actual install parses real XML and ignores comments. A crafted descriptor whose only pre-real <id>...</id> match sits inside a comment passes the gate while the platform reads a foreign plugin id; the dynamic install path passes the zip and the platform-parsed descriptor straight to PluginInstaller.installAndLoadDynamicPlugin with no id comparison of its own, and the restart-script fallback path unpacks the zip's (attacker-named) top-level directory under the plugins root. This defeats the documented 'plugin-id match' invariant of the update-server-to-IDE boundary: a compromised update channel is no longer confined to replacing this plugin but can install content under another plugin's identity. Prerequisite is control of the update channel (manifest or downloadUrl), which already yields arbitrary code as this plugin; the additional gain is planting/replacing a different plugin identity.
claimed_root_cause: checkDescriptorXml validates a regex extraction over raw text (DynamicInstallSupport.kt:182-183) instead of the parsed XML tree the platform consumer uses; the guarantee produced by the gate (id equals PLUGIN_ID) is not the guarantee the consumer assumes (the platform-parsed descriptor id is the visualizer id).

title: Marketplace/compat gate resolves the verifier-cli jar by first-match cache walk, silently ignoring the pinned version whenever multiple versions coexist in the Gradle cache
description: The authoritative release gates (verifyGate and the three verifyMarketplaceVerdict legs that build-plugin.yml's gate job requires before publish) select their verifier-cli jar via walkTopDown().maxDepth(4).filter{verifier-cli-*-all.jar}.firstOrNull() over the Gradle cache module directory, with no comparison against dev-support/verifier-cli-version.txt (pin: 1.411, verified at line 1). CI seeds the pinned jar into a ci-seed subdirectory of the same module dir, and gradle/actions/setup-gradle caches persist older version jars across runs, so multiple versions can coexist and the picked jar depends on unspecified walk order. The only guard, VerifierCliVersionGuardTest, asserts only that the pinned version is among the cached versions (extra versions allowed) and skips on CI and on empty cache by its own documentation. The repository's own comment records a real incident of this walk picking the unintended older 1.409 while 1.410 was expected, and that the two versions produce different verdict outcomes. Consequence: the gate can compute its release-blocking verdict with a verifier version nobody pinned, and the release proceeds green.
claimed_root_cause: The gate's trust handoff from the version pin (dev-support/verifier-cli-version.txt) to the executed verifier binary is not enforced at the resolution site: first-match filesystem walk replaces the pin, and the compensating test does not assert what the gate actually runs.
